ratings_why.fun: Good curve: the knot tanks small early hits for free, Groomer and Cheese-Rind grow it mid game, and Speaker, the Thirty-Two and the Piper give three different late goals worth climbing toward.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because split damage changes how every fight resolves (no tribe moves damage between units), and Tie plus Gossip make other tribes' growth part of your own engine.

verdict_why: The core works; a few rules interactions (zero shares, Piper against the Thirty-Two, the King's Health in the pool) need one clear line each.

points.text: Say whether a unit whose share rounds to 0 has taken damage. Old Gundel, Ticklish Chirper and the pain build's 14-damage example depend on it, and Mill-Chimney Sweep's 1-damage pokes give everyone else a 0 share.
The Piper and the Thirty-Two both act at Start of Combat in reading order. Say whether untying ends the shared Health pool, and whether the King's copied stats survive the untie.
The King Enthroned's copied Health joins the Thirty-Two's pool, so the same Health counts twice. Say that the pool counts each unit's Health before the King copies it.
Knot of Ill Omen mostly makes the enemy tankier against small hits. Adding a payoff, such as your first hit on a tied enemy not being split, would make it a card you take on purpose.
Cold-Shed Tangle is two 1/1s, which lose turn-1 fights. A 1/2 body or a 1/2 Stray would let the seed also hold the early game.

standouts.why: Speaker Brotkrume is a real late-game goal: a full seven-unit knot gaining +3/+3 each every turn is a board you climb toward.
The Piper flips the tribe's own rules for a huge opening volley and gives a real choice against Quorum 7.
Runway Gossip turns other tribes' growth into yours, which makes every pivot and tied neutral pay off.

weakest.why: Knot of Ill Omen often helps the enemy, because their knot also spreads your small hits.
Little Fips is a plain body with no late role.
Cold-Shed Tangle's two 1/1s lose early fights; it only matters as Quorum count.

flags.note: Golden Ilse makes every Gossip in her knot gain all the knot's growth, so two or three Gossips multiply the board's growth each turn. A great high roll, but worth the owner's eye.
The Thirty-Two with the King and Old Gundel: a pool counting copied Health, and Attack that keeps rising on units that can't die.
Supper Sniffer spreading Damage Reduction across a knot, applied per share, can make small hits do nothing.
Mill-Chimney Sweep's 1-damage pokes split into 0 shares; it's unclear what they trigger.
